articles.title: Needle-based Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy (nCLE) for Tool-in-Lesion Confirmation in Cone-Beam CT-guided Navigation Bronchoscopy: a Prospective Concordance Study
articles.authors: van Heumen S, Mets OM, de Bruin DM, Bonta PI, Daniels JMA, Heuvelmans MA, Annema JT
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.summary: Positioning sampling instruments within pulmonary nodules remains a challenge during navigation bronchoscopy. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and needle-based confocal laser endomicroscopy (nCLE) enable tool positioning feedback. However, access to CBCT systems is limited and associated with radiation exposure. To date, no direct comparison between these two modalities has been reported. This study compares CBCT and nCLE for sampling tool position in navigation bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs). Twenty-five patients with PPNs scheduled for CBCT-guided navigation bronchoscopy were prospectively enrolled. …

institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Chimie Physique et Chimie du Vivant
articles.summary: The concentration of biologically relevant metal cations can be monitored with subcellular precision thanks to chemogenetic fluorescent indicators that combine a small molecular probe with a recombinant protein tag, but despite a few reported examples emitting in the blue/green range, such indicators remain underexplored in the case of Zn2+ cations. Using a combination of rational and theoretical design, we report a series of hybrid fluorescent zinc indicators based on a hemicyanine scaffold with a red fluorescence emission. …

articles.title: Time-Resolved Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Profiling of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells Reveals Convergent Immunosuppressive Remodeling in Glioblastoma
articles.authors: Yasodha Kesavan, Haya Tchalabi, Rahul Juluru, Saptrshi Ghosh, Shreya Mattegunta, Saurav Kumar, Sree Deepthi Mutthukrishnan, Basit Khan, James Battiste, Rupa Haldavnekar
articles.summary: Systemic immune dysfunction is a hallmark of glioblastoma (GBM) progression and therapeutic resistance, yet rapid, minimally invasive methods for sensing dynamic immune-cell state changes remain limited. Here, we introduce a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) immune-sensing framework that uses peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) biochemical profiles as an accessible readout of GBM-associated systemic immunosuppression. Ag nanoparticle-decorated black silicon SERS substrates were used to profile PBMCs in GBM−PBMC coculture models representing early and progressed tumor−immune interaction states over 3–72 h. …

articles.summary: Purpose To evaluate longitudinal retinal and choroidal vascular changes after epiretinal membrane (ERM) surgery using SS-OCTA and to compare postoperative trajectories between idiopathic and secondary ERM. Methods In this prospective longitudinal study, eyes with idiopathic and secondary ERM undergoing surgery were evaluated at baseline and at postoperative months 1, 3, 6, and 9. Assessments included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area, superficial and deep capillary plexus vessel density (SCP and DCP VD), subfoveal choroidal thickness (SfCT), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), and choriocapillaris flow metrics. …

articles.title: High‐Efficiency Tomography of High‐Dimensional Spatial Mode Entanglement
articles.authors: Jiaxian Zhao, Min Wang, Junlong Tu, Zhifeng Liu, Yu Ge, Chenghou Tu, Yongnan Li, Hui‐Tian Wang
institutions: National Laboratory of Solid State Microstructures
articles.summary: High‐dimensional (HD) entanglement of photonic spatial modes endows photon pair with greater shared information, enabling secure quantum communication even in noisy environments. However, adequately characterizing HD spatial mode entanglement remains challenging due to the exponential scaling of measurements and data processing complexity. Here, we develop and experimentally demonstrate a physics‐informed neural network for efficient quantum state tomography (QST) of HD spatial mode entanglement. Our method substantially reduces the number of coincidence counts required for QST and enables physics‐informed reconstruction from only two projective measurements. …

articles.summary: The exploration of topological states has emerged as a vibrant frontier across diverse physical systems. Among these, the Möbius strip stands out as a canonical structure that has recently inspired intriguing optical physics. In this work, we extend this concept into the high‐dimensional realm by using an optical analogue—the optical Möbius snail. Specifically, employing a skyrmionic beam as the input field, tight focusing yields a continuous family of Möbius strips that exist in three‐dimensional space, giving rise to a snail‐like polarization topological texture. …
